exposure: Septic complications following critical obstetric conditions
Complicated postpartum endometritis (local complications, pelvic peritonitis)
Group B: Complicated postpartum endometritis (B1: Local complications, B2: Pelvic peritonitis)
Group C: Septic complications following critical obstetric conditions
outcome: Pathogenic microflora isolated from uterine and abdominal cavities
Extent of contamination with a pathogen
Sensitivity of isolated microorganisms to antibacterial drugs
cohort: 123 patients who underwent cesarean section and were treated for suppurative septic postpartum complications between January 2013 and December 2022
finding: The pathogenic microflora in patients with suppurative septic postpartum complications was dominated by S. epidermidis, E. faecalis, E. coli, and E. faecium, with varying degrees of resistance to antibacterial drugs observed.
